```{r}

```

```{r}
happiness_ranking <- read_csv("WHR26_Data_Figure_2.1.csv")
```
```{r}
social_spending <- read_csv("social_spending.csv")
```


Notes:
- Converted the .excel files to .csv. The files were not loading, so I did some googling and found that excel files are not compatible with read_csv. 
- 2021 is the most recent year that has consistent data from the social_spending file. happiness_ranking also has data for countries in 2021. This will be the year I start with. 

happiness_ranking description: 
- Has data for 146 countries in 2021. 
- Formatted as columns in the order of year, rank, country name. There are other columns with information that will probably not be relevant to my project. 

social_spending description:
- Has data for 83 countries in 2021. 
- Formatted as columns in the order of country name and years from 2010-2024. Data from 2024 is incomplete, which is why I won't use it. 
- The formatting is a bit weird. What should be the titles of the columns (country name and years) are actually on the fourth row.
